title: Integrated Anammox Treatment Technologies: A Critical Comparative Review for Sustainable Nitrogen Removal and Energy Recovery
content:
The present review compares six Anammox-based technologies for N removal. MBR-Anammox is the highest in terms of treatment efficiency. BES-Anammox could achieve near energy neutral operation by recovering bioelectricity, while CW-Anammox is the most economical decentralized option. A joint MCDA-SWOT framework shows that no single technology leads in all performance criteria.


ABSTRACT

The anaerobic ammonium oxidation (Anammox) process has revolutionized biological nitrogen removal from wastewater, but is still hampered by slow bacterial growth, sensitivity to temperatures below 15°C and limited mainstream municipal application. The main approach to tackle these issues is to combine Anammox with other complementary technologies. This review compares six integration routes, namely partial nitritation-Anammox (PN-Anammox), bioelectrochemical systems-Anammox (BES-Anammox), constructed wetlands-Anammox (CW-Anammox), membrane bioreactors-Anammox (MBR-Anammox), granular sludge-Anammox (GS-Anammox), and photocatalysis–Anammox (Pho-Anammox). Because these routes overlap (a PN-Anammox process can itself run in a membrane or granular reactor), we organize them in a two-level framework that separates the nitrogen-conversion pathway from the biomass-retention configuration and any coupled auxiliary process, and we state how studies that combine several features were assigned. Five metrics are assessed: nitrogen removal efficiency, energy performance, process stability, cost-effectiveness, and environmental impact. Reported nitrogen removal ranges from 60% to 95%, and much of that spread reflects reactor scale, wastewater type, temperature and reporting practice rather than intrinsic differences between technologies, so the study-level evidence behind each range is now tabulated. Energy performance is reported separately as savings relative to conventional nitrification–denitrification, direct energy recovery, and net energy consumption, each within a stated boundary; on this basis none of the six routes has yet been shown to be a net energy producer at practical scale. A multicriteria decision analysis with a documented scoring procedure and a scenario and Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis is combined with a SWOT assessment. PN-Anammox and CW-Anammox rank highest under most weightings, reflecting mature full-scale evidence and very low energy and cost, respectively. MBR-Anammox gives the highest nitrogen removal but is held back by membrane energy and cost, while BES- and Pho-Anammox rank lowest, mainly because their evidence is still confined to the laboratory. The review highlights critical knowledge gaps and recommends research priorities to expedite trustworthy full-scale implementation.
